extracted.intended_audience: affected employers, industry stakeholders, trade associations, labor organizations, experts, and members of the public invited to comment
extracted.subtask_description: Notice requesting public comment and soliciting specific information via site visits and phone interviews to support economic analysis for a Permissible Exposure Limit (PEL) rulemaking. Collects process-, exposure-, technology-, and cost-related data for affected substances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment: necessity and practical utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information will have practical utility;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a criterion for public comments under the Paperwork Reduction Act: explain how the requested data will be used by OSHA and demonstrate practical utility for the agency's functions or the rulemaking economic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment: accuracy of burden estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden of the proposed collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address OSHA's respondent-counts, hours-per-respondent, cost estimates, and the methods/assumptions that produced those estimates (e.g., typical site visit length, phone interview duration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment: enhance quality, utility, and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest improvements to the content, format, or phrasing of data requests so responses are more precise, useful, or comparable for economic and technological feasibility analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment: minimize respondent burden and use of technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, including the use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology e.g., permitting electronic submissions of responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend ways to reduce time/cost burdens (streamline questions, allow electronic submission, sample strategies) and identify feasible technological collection approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of processes or operations with employee exposures
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of processes or operations that may result in exposures to employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site visits should identify specific processes/operations at the establishment where employees might be exposed to the substance in question (e.g., manufacturing steps, handling operations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of production process and control technology
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of the production process, its technology, and control technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed descriptions of production steps, equipment, current engineering controls (ventilation, enclosures), and any process-specific control technologies in use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of activities by occupation causing exposures
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of activities by occupation that result in worker exposures. How are employees exposed? During what work activities? What is the length and frequency of exposure?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report exposure pathways tied to specific job tasks, task frequency/duration, and circumstances under which exposure occurs (routine vs. episodic). Include task-level detail where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of employees exposed by process and occupation
rubrics_metrics.description: How many employees work in each process with exposures to the substance in question? How many employees are in each occupation at that process?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide headcounts by process and by occupation, including shift patterns, to permit extrapolation of workforce at risk within the establishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available exposure-level data (historical and current)
rubrics_metrics.description: What data is available of exposure levels of each occupation of the process? Is historical data available?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply measured exposure concentrations (personal and area samples), sampling methods, dates, and any historical monitoring data that show trends or variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information on technologies/controls and achievable exposure levels
rubrics_metrics.description: What technology or controls are capable of reducing exposures? What exposure levels could be achieved with other control technologies? Are there substitutes for the substance in question? Are there other technologies employed by the industry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe possible engineering controls, substitution options, best-available technologies, and quantify the exposure reductions achievable with each option where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative controls and work practice changes affecting exposures
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there changes in administrative controls or work practices that could affect employee exposures?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report on scheduling, work rotation, training, housekeeping, PPE policies, and other administrative or procedural measures that can alter exposure profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimates of control and reduction costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates of the cost of the various means of reducing occupational exposure levels. Estimates of the cost of current controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide capital, installation, operation, maintenance, training, and downtime cost estimates for current controls and for potential alternative controls or technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: General establishment information
rubrics_metrics.description: General information from the establishment on number of employees, number of production employees, products and production levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply establishment-size metrics, workforce composition, product types, production volumes/throughput to allow scaling of per-establishment data to industry-level impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-level technology, controls, and exposure information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about the technology, controls, and exposures for the rest of the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide knowledge of common practices across peer firms, industry adoption rates of controls, typical exposure ranges, and whether the visited establishment is representative or atypical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic benefits of exposure-reducing technology
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the economic benefits of installing production technology that reduces exposures?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe productivity gains, reduced injury/illness costs, insurance or compliance benefits, efficiency improvements, or other quantifiable economic advantages associated with control installation.
